title: Continuity Days for Controlled Substance Replacements in Behavioral Health Care
content:
**Pharmacy Benefit — behavioral health coordination clause.** A lost or stolen replacement of a controlled substance for a member in active behavioral health care carries continuity days.

**Clause.** The continuity days are six (6) where the drug is a controlled substance and the member has two or more paid behavioral health visit claims with a service date in the last two months, four (4) where the drug is a controlled substance and the member has exactly one such claim, and nothing otherwise.

The claims read are claims booked on the member's Medicaid Managed Care Membership whose service category is behavioral health visit and whose adjudication status is paid, with a service date in the last two months. The drug is the drug of the replacement; it is a controlled substance when its latest refill carries a DEA schedule (CII to CV). The continuity days are added to the replacement base days.

### Truth table

| Drug is a controlled substance | Paid behavioral health visit claims, last two months | Continuity days |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Two or more | 6 |
| Yes | Exactly one | 4 |
| Yes | None | Nothing |
| No | any | Nothing |
